about: The Brazilian real's settlement calendar: Brazil's national holidays, on which the banks and the Central Bank's PTAX fixing are closed, 1990-2100. New Year's Day (Confraternização Universal); Carnival Monday and Tuesday (48 and 47 days before Easter); Good Friday (Paixão de Cristo); Tiradentes (April 21); Labour Day (May 1); Corpus Christi (60 days after Easter); Independence Day (September 7); Our Lady of Aparecida (October 12); All Souls' Day (Finados, November 2); Proclamation of the Republic (November 15); the National Day of Zumbi and Black Consciousness (November 20, a national holiday from 2024 by Law 14.759 of 2023-12-21); Christmas (December 25). A holiday on a weekend isn't moved, and two on one day are one day. Checked against ANBIMA's national holiday tables for 2001, 2023, 2024 and 2026 (anbima.com.br/feriados, read 2026-10-09); ANBIMA's spreadsheet of every year 2001-2099 is captured raw as BR-ANBIMA. Years before 2001 are the rules unchecked against a published list.
